summary: Both editions were independently compared with the selected Greek throughout all seven paragraphs. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the cleaning and fitting instructions, rejection of unsuitable stones, cutting of most stones, interior/exterior placement and support, two-day interval, mandatory cleanup, and explicit negative consequence. The simplified edition's condensed transitions retain the dialogue's attribution and sequence. Both disclose the bar-marked departure clause as an editorial supplement rather than direct Athos testimony. Acceptance is limited to fidelity to the supplied working source and compatibility with the supplied reports; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, certify editions, or establish exhaustive collation.
